sources.name: Poly Haven

access.notes: No key. Send a User-Agent that names the tool (their API terms require it). /assets?type=hdris|textures|models, /search?q=&t=, /info/{id}, /files/{id}. Counts on 2026-11-14: 997 HDRIs, 869 textures, 522 models.

sources.not_for: Low-poly, toon or pixel games (looks out of place); characters or animals (almost none); anything animated.

The website forbids scraping; use the API only. If the game shows a live Poly Haven browser to players, say "Powered by Poly Haven".
Logos, renders and site text are not CC0; only the assets are.

gotchas: Licence is per sound: CC0, CC BY (Attribution) or CC BY-NC (Attribution NonCommercial). Always filter: NC sounds are not allowed in a commercial game.
API filter for CC0 only: filter=license:"Creative Commons 0". Attribution sounds: filter=license:"Attribution". Never use "Attribution NonCommercial".
CC BY sounds need a credit line per sound (title, author, link, licence). CC0 needs none, but crediting is polite.
The API key belongs to the user: the user must create a free account and apply at https://freesound.org/apiv2/apply, then put the key in .env. The agent must never create accounts.
Original files need OAuth2 (Download Sound is "OAuth2 required"); the token gives HQ previews (preview-hq-ogg ~192 kbps, preview-hq-mp3 ~128 kbps), which are fine for browser games.
Record the sound id, author and licence in the credits file at download time; licences can differ between sounds in the same pack.
sources.credit_template: "{title}" by {author} ({url}), licensed under {license}
sources.license_quote: Some sounds you cannot use commercially, and many of the sounds you need to credit the author.

sources.name: Sonniss GDC Game Audio Bundles

access.notes: no account; multi-GB zip parts per year (GDC 2024 bundle: 9 parts, 23.5 GB); 2026 bundle on gdc.sonniss.com

sources.good_for: Professional-grade sound effects (weapons, foley, ambience, UI, creatures, vehicles) when you want quality without credits.
sources.not_for: Quick agent downloads (parts are several GB each); any AI training; re-sharing the raw sounds.
gotchas: Huge downloads: have the user download one bundle part by hand, then copy only the few files you need into the game. Do not mass-download.
Not a CC licence. Allowed: use and modify in commercial games, no attribution. Forbidden: distributing the files "as sound effects" (no sound packs, no public asset repo of the raw files).
AI/ML training with these sounds is explicitly prohibited.
Files are large 24-bit/96 kHz wavs: trim and convert to ogg/mp3 before shipping.
Keep the bundle licence PDF/text with your project records.
sources.credit_template: No credit required. Optional: "Sound effects from the Sonniss GDC Game Audio Bundle (sonniss.com)"
sources.license_quote: Licensee may use and modify the licensed sound effects for personal and commercial projects

gotchas: Same licence for all packs on the site (not CC): commercial use OK, credit optional, but no redistribution of the raw files, even for free.
If a pack download asks for an email, the user does it; the agent must not sign up.
Some packs include plugins/instruments (not needed for games); use only the audio files.

Credit must be inside the game itself (credits screen), not only on a store page.
Credit format for music: "Music by Eric Matyas" and "www.soundimage.org"; name the track when you mix in other artists.
Use in obscene or pornographic media is prohibited.
Paid non-attribution option exists ($30 per track, $5 per sound effect) if credit is impossible.

access.notes: no key for the CSS API (fonts.googleapis.com/css2) or the GitHub repo; per-family licence file (OFL-1.1, Apache-2.0 or UFL-1.0)

sources.good_for: Every UI and title font need: pixel fonts (Press Start 2P, Silkscreen, VT323), display, handwriting, body text in many scripts.

OFL rules: embed/bundle freely in a game; do not sell the font by itself; ship OFL.txt (copyright + licence) next to the font files; if you modify a font with a Reserved Font Name, rename it.
Self-host the woff2 files instead of linking fonts.googleapis.com: works offline, no third-party request (privacy, GDPR).
The CSS API returns woff2 only when the request looks like a modern browser; with plain curl you may get ttf. Fine either way.

sources.name: Iconify API (index of 270+ open icon sets)

access.notes: no key; search https://api.iconify.design/search?query=...; per-set licence in the "collections" block of every response; SVG at https://api.iconify.design/<prefix>/<name>.svg

sources.good_for: Agents finding an icon by keyword across hundreds of sets and reading the licence from the same response (game-icons, Lucide, Tabler, Phosphor, Material, pixelarticons, Twemoji, Noto emoji...).
sources.not_for: Trusting the licence field blindly for sets that changed licence recently (see gotchas).
gotchas: Licence is per icon set: read collections[prefix].license.spdx. On 2026-11-14 the 276 sets were mostly MIT (144), CC-BY-4.0 (53), Apache-2.0 (31), OFL-1.1 (13), CC0 (10), but also CC-BY-SA (9), GPL (6) and CC-BY-NC (2). Allow-list SPDX ids; reject NC, and avoid SA/GPL unless the user accepts share-alike.
Restrict searches with prefixes= to sets you already approved, e.g. prefixes=game-icons,lucide,tabler,ph,pixelarticons.

The licence field can lag upstream: Iconify still listed Remix Icon as Apache 2.0, but upstream switched to its own "Remix Icon License v1.0" in Jan 2026. Check the set's own repo for anything you ship.
CC BY sets (game-icons, Font Awesome, Twemoji) need credit; record the author per icon.
Public API is a shared free service: fetch the few icons you need and save the SVGs into the repo; do not call it at game runtime or in bulk.

api.iconify.design robots.txt disallows crawlers (and says ai-train=no): make single lookups and cache them, never crawl. For offline use install @iconify-json/<prefix> (one npm package per set, with licence metadata).

sources.good_for: Auto-rigging a humanoid and adding walk/run/jump/attack/idle animations for a 3D browser game.
sources.not_for: Non-humanoid characters (biped humanoids only); redistributing animation files as an asset pack.
gotchas: Needs an Adobe account. The agent cannot log in or download for the user: the user uploads/downloads by hand and puts the FBX files in the project.
Royalty-free in commercial games, no credit, but raw character/animation files must not be redistributed on their own (no "animation pack" or template that ships the raw files as the product).
Export FBX, then convert to glb in Blender (merge animations into one file, check scale and root motion).
Licence page blocks scripted fetching; the quote was confirmed through Adobe's help page text in search results on 2026-11-14.
sources.credit_template: No credit required.
sources.license_quote: You can use both characters and animations royalty free for personal, commercial, and non-profit projects

tools.name: Blender
tools.what: 3D modelling, sculpting, rigging, animation, rendering; converts FBX/OBJ to glTF/glb; scriptable headless with Python.
tools.output_license: yours (the GPL covers the program, not the files you make)
tools.good_for: Converting and cleaning any 3D asset to .glb, decimating, baking textures, merging Mixamo clips.
tools.notes: Runs on mac, win and linux. Agents can drive it headless: `blender -b -P script.py`.

tools.name: Krita
tools.good_for: Painted sprites, backgrounds, UI art, frame-by-frame animation.
tools.notes: mac, win, linux. The store versions (Steam, Microsoft Store) cost money; the krita.org download is free.

tools.name: GIMP
tools.good_for: Cropping, recolouring, making texture atlases, batch edits (Script-Fu/Python).
tools.notes: mac, win, linux. For quick scripted edits ImageMagick or sharp is easier for agents.

tools.name: Inkscape
tools.what: Vector (SVG) editor with a command line exporter.
tools.good_for: Editing SVG icons and UI, exporting PNGs at any size: `inkscape in.svg --export-type=png --export-width=256`.
tools.notes: mac, win, linux. Development moved to GitLab (gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape).

tools.name: Blockbench
tools.what: Low-poly / blocky 3D model and animation editor with a web app (web.blockbench.net).
tools.output_license: yours; site says it is "free to use for any type of project, forever, no strings attached"
tools.good_for: Low-poly and voxel-like characters and props with simple animations; exports glTF via its exporters.
tools.notes: Also desktop for mac, win, linux. Pixel-art textures painted inside the app.

tools.name: MagicaVoxel
tools.what: Voxel model editor and path-traced renderer.
tools.output_license: yours; site says "Free to use for any project." (redistributing the app itself is not allowed)
tools.good_for: Voxel characters, props and scenes; exports .vox, .obj, .ply, PNG renders.
tools.notes: mac and win only. Convert .obj to .glb in Blender. Last release 0.99.7.x (2023).

tools.name: Goxel
tools.good_for: Voxel modelling on Linux or when an open-source tool is required; exports .vox, .obj, .gltf, .ply, PNG.
tools.notes: Also mac, win, and a web build. Paid store versions exist on some app stores; the source build is free.

tools.name: LDtk (Level Designer Toolkit)
tools.what: 2D level editor from the director of Dead Cells.
tools.good_for: Tile/entity levels for 2D games; exports documented JSON, "Super Simple Export" PNG layers + JSON, optional Tiled TMX.
tools.notes: mac, win, linux. Site: "LDtk can be used for free without any limitation."

tools.name: Tiled Map Editor
tools.good_for: Tile maps for Phaser, PixiJS, Excalibur, etc. (export JSON, TMX).
tools.notes: mac, win, linux. itch.io page lets users pay optionally; download is free. Phaser loads Tiled JSON natively.

tools.name: Aseprite
tools.output_license: yours (EULA does not claim your artwork)
tools.good_for: Best-in-class pixel sprite animation, sprite sheet + JSON export, CLI batch export (`aseprite -b in.aseprite --sheet out.png --data out.json`).
tools.notes: mac, win, linux. Paid binaries ($19.99 on site/Steam). Source is on GitHub; the EULA allows compiling for "your own personal purpose" only and forbids distributing copies. Free alternative: LibreSprite (fork of the old GPL version) or Pixelorama.

tools.name: LibreSprite
tools.what: Free fork of Aseprite from before its licence change.
tools.good_for: Aseprite-like pixel animation for free.
tools.notes: mac, win, linux. Fewer features than current Aseprite.

tools.name: Pixelorama
tools.what: Pixel-art editor and animator built with Godot; desktop and web.
tools.good_for: Pixel sprites, tilesets and animations; exports PNG, sprite sheets, GIF.
tools.notes: Also mac, win, linux builds. MIT means it can even be embedded.

tools.name: Piskel
tools.good_for: Quick pixel sprites and small animations, export PNG sprite sheet or GIF; easiest for absolute beginners.
tools.notes: Offline desktop builds exist. No account needed to draw and export.

tools.name: Material Maker
tools.good_for: Tileable PBR textures (base colour, normal, roughness) for 3D games.
tools.notes: win, linux, mac builds on GitHub/itch. Export PNG maps, load in three.js MeshStandardMaterial.

tools.name: ArmorPaint
tools.good_for: Painting textures directly on a 3D model.
tools.notes: Ready-made builds cost $19 (download page, refund policy). The source (github.com/armory3d/armorpaint, zlib licence) is free to build yourself, which is not beginner-friendly. mac, win, linux.

tools.name: MakeHuman (app)
tools.output_license: CC0 for exports made with the bundled assets
tools.good_for: Rigged realistic human bases; see the makehuman source entry.
tools.notes: mac, win, linux; MPFB add-on for Blender. Community add-on assets may be CC BY.

tools.name: VRoid Studio (pixiv)
tools.output_license: yours; official guidelines allow commercial use of models made from VRoid Studio's own meshes, textures and presets "provided that no special clauses are indicated in the license"
tools.good_for: Anime/stylised humanoid characters for three.js (load VRM with @pixiv/three-vrm).
tools.notes: mac and win (Steam too). Third-party presets/textures from BOOTH etc. carry their own terms, often with credit or no-commercial rules: check each. The guidelines page blocked scripted fetching; verified via search excerpt of vroid.com/en/studio/guidelines on 2026-11-14. Set the VRM export permission fields yourself.

tools.name: Audacity
tools.good_for: Trimming, normalising, looping and converting sound effects and music to ogg/mp3.
tools.notes: mac, win, linux. For scripted batch conversion use ffmpeg instead.

tools.name: LMMS
tools.what: Free digital audio workstation (pattern/piano-roll music maker with built-in synths).
tools.output_license: yours (check licences of any third-party sample packs or plugins you add)
tools.good_for: Full game soundtracks by a user who wants more than BeepBox; exports wav/ogg/mp3.
tools.notes: mac, win, linux.

tools.name: Bfxr / Bfxr2
tools.what: sfxr-style retro sound effect generator in the browser with extra synth options.
tools.output_license: not stated on the site; generally treated as yours (sounds are synthesised from your settings)
tools.good_for: Retro jump/coin/laser/explosion sounds with more control than jsfxr; exports wav.
tools.notes: Kept in tools, not sources, because neither bfxr.net nor the bfxr2 README states the licence of generated sounds (checked 2026-11-14). jsfxr or ChipTone have explicit statements.

tools.name: LabChirp
tools.what: Sound effect generator (Windows .NET; Mono on mac/linux).
tools.good_for: Synth/retro sound effects with more parameters than sfxr.
tools.notes: No output licence statement (checked 2026-11-14), so prefer jsfxr/ChipTone/ZzFX in the kit.

tools.name: FFmpeg
tools.good_for: Agent-friendly conversion of wav/mp3 to ogg/mp3/m4a, trimming, loudness normalisation (`ffmpeg -i in.wav -af loudnorm -c:a libvorbis -q:a 4 out.ogg`).
tools.notes: mac (brew install ffmpeg), win, linux.

avoid.name: Pixabay (images, music, sound effects)
avoid.why: Kit policy: Pixabay Content License is not a Creative Commons licence and restricts standalone redistribution (a public game repo with the raw files can count). Use CC0/CC BY sources instead.
avoid.quote: You cannot sell or distribute Content (either in digital or physical form) on a Standalone basis.

avoid.name: Mixkit (Envato) music and sound effects
avoid.why: Kit policy: custom Mixkit licences (not CC), some items are personal-use only ("Restricted License"), and raw items may not be resold/redistributed unaltered.
avoid.license_seen: Mixkit Free License / Mixkit Restricted License (custom)
avoid.quote: Only allows use in personal, non-commercial projects. (Restricted License, from mixkit.co/llm-info)

avoid.name: Shadertoy shaders
avoid.why: Shaders without an explicit licence from the author default to CC BY-NC-SA 3.0: no commercial use, share-alike. Only copy a shader whose header states a permissive licence (MIT, CC0).
avoid.license_seen: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 by default (terms page sits behind a bot check; default confirmed via shader headers and secondary sources)
avoid.quote: License Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License.

avoid.name: LYGIA shader library
avoid.why: Dual licensed: Prosperity Public License 3.0.0 (non-commercial; commercial use only as a 30-day trial) or the Patron License for GitHub sponsors/contributors. A commercial game needs sponsorship or a paid licence.
avoid.quote: This license allows you to use and share this software for noncommercial purposes for free and to try this software for commercial purposes for thirty days.

avoid.name: BBC Sound Effects archive
avoid.why: RemArc licence: personal, educational and research use only; commercial use needs a paid licence (via Pro Sound Effects). Site could not be fetched by our tools; terms confirmed through news coverage quoting the licence.
avoid.quote: the Sound Effects are BBC copyright, but they may be used for personal, educational or research purposes

avoid.name: Tabletop Audio
avoid.why: Ambiences are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: no commercial use and no modification. Patreon covers podcast/video use only.

avoid.name: Any asset marked NC or ND (on any site: Sketchfab, Freesound, FMA, ccMixter, itch.io, OpenGameArt...)
avoid.why: NC forbids commercial use (a game with ads, a price, donations or sponsorship counts). ND forbids distributing modified versions (resizing, recolouring, cutting a loop may count). Sketchfab CC BY / CC0 models are fine; its NC, ND and "Editorial" models are not.
avoid.license_seen: CC BY-NC, CC BY-NC-SA, CC BY-ND, CC BY-NC-ND; Sketchfab Editorial
avoid.quote: NonCommercial — You may not use the material for commercial purposes.

avoid.name: ZapSplat
avoid.why: Needs an account (user must sign up), own Standard License (not CC), free tier requires credit and limits downloads; licence page returned 403 to our fetcher, so terms are unverified. Not agent-friendly.
avoid.license_seen: ZapSplat Standard License (custom); unverified on site
avoid.quote: unverified: site blocked automated fetch on 2026-11-14

avoid.name: Fab (Epic) free and "limited-time free" assets
avoid.why: Not an open licence: needs an Epic account (agent cannot download), proprietary Standard License forbids redistributing assets standalone (a public repo of raw files is risky). Note: the current Fab licence summary does NOT limit use to Unreal Engine; we found no "UE-only" clause on 2026-11-14.
avoid.quote: Resell or redistribute the asset for free on a standalone basis or allow others to do the same.

avoid.name: Unity Asset Store free assets
avoid.why: Account-gated, proprietary EULA: assets licensed only as an embedded component of your product, users may not be enabled to extract/distribute them, publishers can attach extra "Restricted Asset" terms. The EULA text does not mention other engines either way. Not usable by an agent and risky in an open repo.
avoid.quote: as an embedded component of that Licensed Product

avoid.name: TurboSquid free models (and Free3D, run by TurboSquid)
avoid.why: Royalty Free License requires that end users cannot import/export 3D models; secondary summaries list browser-based games as prohibited. A web game ships the .glb to the browser, so it is a poor fit. Free3D uses the same licence plus per-model "Personal Use" labels.
avoid.license_seen: TurboSquid Royalty Free License; Free3D Personal Use / Royalty Free (per model)
avoid.quote: The software or game has no functionality for end users to import any open 3D file format or export any 3D model.

avoid.name: CGTrader free models
avoid.why: Free models use whatever licence the seller picks; the Royalty Free License allows games but requires protecting the model from end-user access (proprietary/encrypted format). Plain .glb files in a browser game do not meet that. Some free models are Editorial-only.
avoid.license_seen: CGTrader Royalty Free License / Editorial (per model)
avoid.quote: you must take all commercially reasonable measures to prevent the end user from gaining access to the Product.

avoid.name: Envato Elements (incl. free monthly files)
avoid.why: Subscription licence, registered per project: items can no longer be used in new projects after the subscription ends, and each use must be registered. Not an open licence; account-gated. Help page blocked our fetcher; terms confirmed from Envato help-centre text in search results.
avoid.quote: you cannot use downloaded items to create new end products after your subscription ends

avoid.name: "Royalty free" / "no copyright" music on YouTube channels and similar sites
avoid.why: Usually no written licence, licences scoped to YouTube videos only (YouTube Audio Library), or Content ID claims later. "Royalty free" is not a licence. Use incompetech, Freesound, FMA (filtered) or make music with BeepBox.
avoid.quote: n/a: no licence text to quote; that absence is the problem

avoid.name: Ready Player Me avatars
avoid.why: Service shut down: the public platform, avatar creator and developer APIs/SDKs closed on 31 Jan 2026 after Netflix acquired the company (Dec 2025). The domain no longer resolved on 2026-11-14. Use VRoid Studio, MakeHuman or a Blockbench character instead.

avoid.name: FreePD.com (public-domain music)
avoid.why: Site permanently closed (2008-2025); mirrors and re-uploads cannot be verified. Use incompetech (CC BY) or Freesound CC0 music loops instead.
avoid.quote: Public Domain music downloads (site now states hosting and maintenance have ceased)
